claim: The first instar Drosophila melanogaster larval central nervous system (CNS) is composed of an estimated 10,000 cells.
source: The first instar Drosophila melanogaster larval central nervous system (CNS) is composed of an estimated 10,000 cells (Scott et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Scott et al., 2001.

claim: Only 2000 of the cells in the first instar larval CNS populate the two larval cerebral lobes.
source: Only 2000 of these cells populate the two larval cerebral lobes, the remaining cells are distributed among segmental ganglia of the ventral nerve cord (VNC).
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text following the citation about total cell number.

claim: The cells populating the larval brain develop from neuroblasts delaminated from the procephalic neurectoderm during early embryonic stages.
source: The cells populating the larval brain develop from neuroblasts delaminated from the procephalic neurectoderm, during early embryonic stages.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text as established knowledge about larval brain development.

claim: At the end of embryogenesis neurons are fully differentiated and form the functional neural circuits of the larval brain.
source: At the end of embryogenesis neurons are fully differentiated and form the functional neural circuits of the larval brain, while neuroblasts enter a mitotic quiescence phase and are only reactivated at the end of the first larval instar.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text as established knowledge about developmental timing.

claim: Neuroblasts enter a mitotic quiescence phase at the end of embryogenesis and are only reactivated at the end of the first larval instar.
source: At the end of embryogenesis neurons are fully differentiated and form the functional neural circuits of the larval brain, while neuroblasts enter a mitotic quiescence phase and are only reactivated at the end of the first larval instar.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text as established knowledge about neuroblast quiescence.

claim: Some glial cells in close proximity to neuroblast populations release insulin-like peptides upon nutrient-sensing.
source: It has been previously described that some glial cells, in close proximity to the neuroblast populations, release insulin-like peptides upon nutrient-sensing. This signal is later incorporated by neuroblasts through the InR/PI3K/TORC1 pathway, to ultimately induce reactivation and exit from quiescence (Chell and Brand, 2010; Sousa-Nunes et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Chell and Brand, 2010 and Sousa-Nunes et al., 2011.

claim: Insulin-like peptide signals from glial cells are incorporated by neuroblasts through the InR/PI3K/TORC1 pathway to induce reactivation and exit from quiescence.
source: It has been previously described that some glial cells, in close proximity to the neuroblast populations, release insulin-like peptides upon nutrient-sensing. This signal is later incorporated by neuroblasts through the InR/PI3K/TORC1 pathway, to ultimately induce reactivation and exit from quiescence (Chell and Brand, 2010; Sousa-Nunes et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Chell and Brand, 2010 and Sousa-Nunes et al., 2011.

claim: At late-larval stages, NPCs can proliferate even in aversive feeding conditions, independently of the InR/PI3K/TORC1 signaling pathway.
source: Surprisingly, at late-larval stages, NPCs seem to be able to proliferate even in aversive feeding conditions, independently of the InR/PI3K/TORC1 signaling pathway (Cheng et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Cheng et al., 2011.

claim: The study obtained a cell atlas of the first instar larval brain with a total of 9353 cells and a median of 1658 genes per cell.
source: We obtained a cell atlas of the first instar larval brain with a total of 9353 cells and a median of 1658 genes per cell.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text describing the dataset obtained.

claim: The normal feeding dataset comprised 4708 cells with a median of 1434 genes per cell and 836,393 mean reads per cell.
source: In summary, the normal dataset comprised 4708 cells with a median of 1434 genes per cell and 836,393 mean reads per cell.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text describing the normal feeding dataset.

claim: The starvation dataset comprised 4645 cells with a median of 1962 genes per cell and 545,512 mean reads per cell.
source: While the starvation dataset comprised 4645 cells with a median of 1962 genes per cell and 545,512 mean reads per cell (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text describing the starvation dataset.

claim: Five major cell-type categories were distinguished in the larval brain: differentiated neurons, NPCs, glial cells, undifferentiated neurons and a group of non-neural cells.
source: Among the 29 clusters, we distinguished five main cell type categories: differentiated neurons, NPCs, glial cells, undifferentiated neurons and a group of non-neural cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 1B showing the five cell type categories.

claim: Differentiated neurons can be defined by the expression of the pan-neuronal marker embryonic lethal abnormal vision (elav).
source: Differentiated neurons could be defined by the expression of the pan-neuronal marker embryonic lethal abnormal vision (elav), presynaptic genes or widely expressed neurotransmitters, NPCs by Notch (N) or deadpan (dpn) expression, and glial cells by the expression of reversed polarity (repo) (Figure 1C,D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 1C and 1D showing elav expression.

claim: NPCs can be defined by Notch (N) or deadpan (dpn) expression.
source: Differentiated neurons could be defined by the expression of the pan-neuronal marker embryonic lethal abnormal vision (elav), presynaptic genes or widely expressed neurotransmitters, NPCs by Notch (N) or deadpan (dpn) expression, and glial cells by the expression of reversed polarity (repo) (Figure 1C,D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 1C and 1D showing Notch and dpn expression.

claim: Glial cells can be defined by the expression of reversed polarity (repo).
source: Differentiated neurons could be defined by the expression of the pan-neuronal marker embryonic lethal abnormal vision (elav), presynaptic genes or widely expressed neurotransmitters, NPCs by Notch (N) or deadpan (dpn) expression, and glial cells by the expression of reversed polarity (repo) (Figure 1C,D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 1C and 1D showing repo expression.

claim: The early temporal cascade gene Kr was observed to be expressed in differentiated cells.
source: The early cascade gene Kr was observed to be expressed in differentiated cells, while the late gene grh was almost exclusively expressed in cells from the neurogenic clusters (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 2A showing Kr expression pattern.

claim: The late temporal cascade gene grh was almost exclusively expressed in cells from the neurogenic clusters.
source: The early cascade gene Kr was observed to be expressed in differentiated cells, while the late gene grh was almost exclusively expressed in cells from the neurogenic clusters (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 2A showing grh expression pattern.

claim: A high number of NPCs express long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs).
source: Interestingly, we detected a high number of cells expressing long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs); some of them with reported functions, as it was the case of cherub (lncRNA:CR43283), known to be involved in tumorigenesis and in normal brain development (Landskron et al., 2018; Malin and Desplan, 2018), but also lncRNAs with unknown functions, like lncRNA:CR30009 (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 2C showing lncRNA expression.

claim: Cherub (lncRNA:CR43283) is known to be involved in tumorigenesis and in normal brain development.
source: Interestingly, we detected a high number of cells expressing long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs); some of them with reported functions, as it was the case of cherub (lncRNA:CR43283), known to be involved in tumorigenesis and in normal brain development (Landskron et al., 2018; Malin and Desplan, 2018), but also lncRNAs with unknown functions, like lncRNA:CR30009 (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Landskron et al., 2018 and Malin and Desplan, 2018.

claim: Genes actively transcribed in the optic lobe neuroepithelium include Ocho (Ocho), Twin of m4 (Tom) and Bearded (Brd).
source: In parallel, we observed expression of genes reported to be actively transcribed in the optic lobe neuroepithelium, such as Ocho (Ocho), Twin of m4 (Tom) and Bearded (Brd) (Egger et al., 2010) in a subpopulation of cells; therefore, this group of cells was annotated as the optic lobe epithelium (OLE) (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Egger et al., 2010 and Figure 2D showing expression of these genes.

claim: A larger number of NPCs were found in G1 and G2/M phases compared to S phase.
source: We found a larger number of cells in G1 and G2/M phases, in comparison to S phase (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 2E showing cell cycle phase distribution.

claim: G2 phase was shown to be an entry point to quiescence, alongside G0 phase.
source: These results further support recent observations, where G2 phase was shown to be an entry point to quiescence, alongside G0 phase (Otsuki and Brand, 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Otsuki and Brand, 2018.

claim: Approximately 30% of dpn positive cells were EdU positive at 16 hr ALH.
source: Therefore, we performed EdU incorporation experiments, together with dpn immunostaining, and identified approximately 30% of dpn positive EdU positive cells, from the total of dpn positive cells (Figure 2F); suggesting that at 16 hr ALH (after larval hatching) some NPCs were already exiting their dormant state and reassuming proliferation.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 2F showing EdU incorporation data.

claim: At 16 hr ALH some NPCs were already exiting their dormant state and reassuming proliferation.
source: Therefore, we performed EdU incorporation experiments, together with dpn immunostaining, and identified approximately 30% of dpn positive EdU positive cells, from the total of dpn positive cells (Figure 2F); suggesting that at 16 hr ALH (after larval hatching) some NPCs were already exiting their dormant state and reassuming proliferation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the EdU incorporation data showing active DNA replication in NPCs.

claim: Glutamate and acetylcholine were found to be the most abundant neurotransmitters, each expressed in 24% of the total number of neurons.
source: Glu and Ach were found to be the most abundant neurotransmitters, as they were each expressed in 24% of the total number of neurons.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text based on analysis of neurotransmitter expression.

claim: GABAergic neurons occupied 17% of the total number of neurons.
source: GABAergic and monoaminergic neurons occupied the third and fourth place, with 17% and 10% of the total number of neurons, respectively. (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 3A-B.

claim: Monoaminergic neurons occupied 10% of the total number of neurons.
source: GABAergic and monoaminergic neurons occupied the third and fourth place, with 17% and 10% of the total number of neurons, respectively. (Figure 3A–B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 3A-B.

claim: Dual-transmitter neurons were more frequent than triple-transmitter neurons.
source: Dual-transmitter neurons were more frequent than triple-transmitter neurons, with the three highest overlap occurring between VGlut and Vmat (3%), followed by VGlut and VAChT (2%) and VGlut and Gad1 (2%).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text based on analysis of co-expression patterns.

claim: The highest overlap of dual-transmitter neurons occurred between VGlut and Vmat (3%).
source: Dual-transmitter neurons were more frequent than triple-transmitter neurons, with the three highest overlap occurring between VGlut and Vmat (3%), followed by VGlut and VAChT (2%) and VGlut and Gad1 (2%).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text based on analysis of co-expression patterns.

claim: Triple-transmitter expressing neurons represent approximately 1% of the total of neurons.
source: Triple-transmitter expressing neurons only represent approximately 1% of the total of neurons (Figure 3C–E).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 3C-E.

claim: An overlapping between VGlut and pale (ple) was observed in immunostainings.
source: We observed an overlapping between VGlut and pale (ple), a tyrosine hydroxylase involved in the synthesis of dopamine (Neckameyer and Quinn, 1989); as well as between VGlut and Gad1 and VAChT and Gad1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 1 showing immunostaining data.

claim: Pale (ple) is a tyrosine hydroxylase involved in the synthesis of dopamine.
source: We observed an overlapping between VGlut and pale (ple), a tyrosine hydroxylase involved in the synthesis of dopamine (Neckameyer and Quinn, 1989); as well as between VGlut and Gad1 and VAChT and Gad1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Neckameyer and Quinn, 1989.

claim: A subset of neurons actively co-expressed different neurotransmitters in the Drosophila larval brain.
source: Thereby, a subset of neurons actively co-expressed different neurotransmitters, showing that this phenomenon also occurs in the Drosophila larval brain.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text based on immunostaining validation of co-expression.

claim: Only Ddc and ple were expressed at high levels in monoaminergic neurons.
source: Interestingly, only Ddc and ple were expressed at high levels in monoaminergic neurons, therefore this cluster was labeled as dopaminergic neurons (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 2A showing expression patterns.

claim: The larval brain possesses five lateral neurons (LNs) per hemisphere, of which only four express the neuropeptide Pigment-dispersing factor (Pdf).
source: Knowing that the larval brain possesses five lateral neurons (LNs) per hemisphere, of which only four express the neuropeptide Pigment-dispersing factor (Pdf) (Collins et al., 2012; Helfrich-Förster, 1997), we decided to further characterize this cell-type.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Collins et al., 2012 and Helfrich-Förster, 1997.

claim: PDF neurons express core clock component genes: cryptochrome (cry), period (per), clock (clk) and timeless (tim).
source: We distinguished the Pdf-LNs of the larval brain, and in addition to Pdf, these cells expressed core clock component genes: cryptochrome (cry), period (per), clock (clk) and timeless (tim).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text based on analysis of gene expression in PDF neurons.

claim: PDF neurons express the Pigment-dispersing factor receptor (Pdfr), suggesting a self-regulatory function for Pdf secretion.
source: In addition, PDF neurons also expressed the Pigment-dispersing factor receptor (Pdfr), suggesting a self-regulatory function for Pdf secretion.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text with an inference about self-regulation based on receptor expression.

claim: Genes implicated in circadian processes are co-expressed with Pdf, including the nuclear hormone receptors Hr51 and Hr38, and the transcription factor vrille (vri).
source: Moreover, genes implicated in circadian processes showed to be co-expressed with Pdf, as it was the case for the nuclear hormone receptors, Hr51 and Hr38, and the transcription factor vrille (vri) (Abruzzi et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by a citation to Abruzzi et al., 2017.

claim: Novel marker genes for PDF neurons include CrebA, Mmp2, AstC-R2 and the transcription factor stripe (sr).
source: Furthermore, we identified novel marker genes for this particular cell-type, some of them with described functions, such as the Cyclic-AMP response element binding protein A (CrebA), Matrix metalloproteinase 2 (Mmp2), Allatostatin C receptor 2 (AstC-R2) and the transcription factor stripe (sr); as well as other uncategorized genes, such as CG11221, CG44153, CG43902 and CG12541 (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 4B showing expression of these genes.

claim: Insulin producing cells (IPCs) are responsible for the synthesis of 3 main insulin like peptides (Ilps): Ilp2, Ilp3 and Ilp5.
source: Following the previous analyses, we then focused on another neurosecretory cell-type, the insulin producing cells (IPCs). These cells are responsible for the synthesis of 3 main insulin like peptides (Ilps): Ilp2, Ilp3 and Ilp5 (Nässel and Vanden Broeck, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Nässel and Vanden Broeck, 2016.

claim: Amon mRNA levels were significantly high in the IPCs found in the larval brain.
source: Additionally, some neuropeptides are known to require the peptidase amontillado (amon) in order to become bioactive, we checked if this was also the case for the Ilps and noticed that amon mRNA levels were significantly high in the IPCs found in the larval brain (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 4D showing amon expression.

claim: An overlap between Crz and Corazonin receptor (CrzR) was not observed in CRZ neurons.
source: Next, we identified a set of neurons involved in the release of Corazonin (Crz), the CRZ neurons. However, in contrast to Pdf-expressing neurons, we did not observe an overlap between Crz and Corazonin receptor (CrzR) in these cells.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text based on analysis of gene expression in CRZ neurons.

claim: The short neuropeptide F (sNPF) is co-synthesized in Crz positive cells.
source: In addition, we observed the short neuropeptide F (sNPF) being co-synthesized in Crz positive cells, as it has been previously described (Johard et al., 2008; Lee et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations to Johard et al., 2008 and Lee et al., 2004.

claim: sNPF exhibits a wide expression in the larval brain.
source: Nevertheless, sNPF has been reported to exhibit a wide expression in the larval brain (Nässel et al., 2008), and in addition to its expression in Crz neurons, it was also expressed in the mushroom body Kenyon cells (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Nässel et al., 2008 and Figure 5B showing expression pattern.

claim: PDF neurons were mostly glutamatergic.
source: We observed that PDF neurons were mostly glutamatergic, while IPCs, PTTH and CRZ neurons seemed to be more promiscuous, co-releasing different neurotransmitters.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text based on analysis of neurotransmitter expression in peptidergic neurons.

claim: IPCs, PTTH and CRZ neurons are promiscuous, co-releasing different neurotransmitters.
source: We observed that PDF neurons were mostly glutamatergic, while IPCs, PTTH and CRZ neurons seemed to be more promiscuous, co-releasing different neurotransmitters.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text based on analysis of neurotransmitter expression in peptidergic neurons.

claim: In the adult fly each mushroom body consists of approximately 2000 neurons called Kenyon cells (KCs).
source: In the adult fly each MB consists of approximately 2000 neurons, called Kenyon cells (KCs), these cells are produced by four mushroom body neuroblasts (MBNBs) per hemisphere, that arise during embryogenesis and continue dividing until pupal stages (Kunz et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kunz et al., 2012.

claim: Kenyon cells are produced by four mushroom body neuroblasts (MBNBs) per hemisphere that arise during embryogenesis and continue dividing until pupal stages.
source: In the adult fly each MB consists of approximately 2000 neurons, called Kenyon cells (KCs), these cells are produced by four mushroom body neuroblasts (MBNBs) per hemisphere, that arise during embryogenesis and continue dividing until pupal stages (Kunz et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kunz et al., 2012.

claim: The neurons populating the larval mushroom body are embryonic-born Kenyon cells.
source: The neurons populating the larval MB, are embryonic-born KCs (Pauls et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Pauls et al., 2010.

claim: Three types of cells were identified in the mushroom body based on cell-cycle phases and marker genes: mushroom body Kenyon cells (MBKCs), mushroom body neuroblasts (MBNBs) and cells undergoing differentiation (MBUNs).
source: We first sub-clustered the population identified as mushroom body, identifying three types of cells based on cell-cycle phases and marker genes: mushroom body Kenyon cells (MBKCs), mushroom body neuroblasts (MBNBs) and cells undergoing differentiation (MBUNs) (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 5A showing the three cell types.

claim: MBKCs express characteristic MB receptors: Dopamine 1-like receptor 1 (Dop1R1), Dopamine 1-like receptor 2 (Dop1R2) and Dopamine 2-like receptor (Dop2R).
source: MBKCs expressed characteristic MB receptors: Dopamine 1-like receptor 1 (Dop1R1); Dopamine 1-like receptor 2 (Dop1R2) and Dopamine 2-like receptor (Dop2R).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text based on analysis of gene expression in MBKCs.

claim: MBKCs are enriched for Fasciclin 2 (Fas2), short neuropeptide F (sNPF) and Neprilysin 1 (Nep1).
source: In addition, these cells were enriched for Fasciclin 2 (Fas2), short neuropeptide F (sNPF) and Neprilysin 1 (Nep1), among other genes (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 5B showing expression of these genes.

claim: Portabella (prt), an orphan vesicular transporter, was previously reported to be expressed in the mushroom body.
source: Remarkably, portabella (prt), an orphan vesicular transporter previously reported to be expressed in the mushroom body (Brooks et al., 2011), was enriched in the larval KCs (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Brooks et al., 2011.

claim: Portabella (prt) was enriched in the larval Kenyon cells.
source: Remarkably, portabella (prt), an orphan vesicular transporter previously reported to be expressed in the mushroom body (Brooks et al., 2011), was enriched in the larval KCs (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 5B showing prt expression.

claim: An accumulation of prt was observed in the MBKCs, more precisely in the calyx, penduncle, and vertical and medial lobes.
source: We confirmed this finding by immunostaining, where we observed an accumulation of prt in the MBKCs, more precisely in the calyx, penduncle, and vertical and medial lobes (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 5C showing immunostaining data.

claim: MBKCs are cholinergic (VAChT).
source: As expected, MBKCs appeared to be cholinergic (VAChT).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text based on analysis of VAChT expression.

claim: MBNBs were found to be constantly proliferating, as indicated by their cell-cycle scores.
source: On the other hand, MBNBs were found to be constantly proliferating, as their cell-cycle scores indicated (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 5A showing cell cycle analysis.

claim: MBNBs express characteristic neuroprogenitor marker genes, such as N, asense (ase), Delta (Dl) and tailless (tll).
source: Moreover, these cells expressed characteristic neuroprogenitor marker genes, such as N, asense (ase), Delta (Dl) and tailless (tll).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text based on analysis of gene expression in MBNBs.

claim: Target of Poxn (tap), a gene playing a key role during mushroom body development, was upregulated in MBNBs.
source: In addition, target of Poxn (tap), a gene playing a key role during mushroom body development was also upregulated in this cell population (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 5B showing tap expression.

claim: MBUNs express the neuronal markers nSyb and VAChT, but at lower levels compared to MBKCs.
source: Finally, MBUNs expressed the neuronal markers, nSyb and VAChT, but at lower levels in comparison to MBKCs, indicating that they are not yet fully differentiated.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text based on analysis of gene expression in MBUNs.

claim: Three different glial cell clusters were observed: astrocytes/neuropil glia, cortex/chiasm glia and surface glia.
source: We observed three different clusters: astrocytes/neuropil glia, cortex/chiasm glia and surface glia, enriched for specific marker genes (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 6A showing the three glial cell types.

claim: Astrocytes like glia were identified based on expression of known marker genes: astrocyte leucine-rich repeat molecule (alrm), Excitatory amino acid transporter 1 (Eaat1), GABA transporter (Gat), Glutamine synthetase 2 (Gs2) and wunen-2 (wun2).
source: Astrocytes like glia were identified based on expression of known marker genes: astrocyte leucine-rich repeat molecule (alrm), Excitatory amino acid transporter 1 (Eaat1), GABA transporter (Gat), Glutamine synthetase 2 (Gs2) and wunen-2 (wun2) (Huang et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by a citation to Huang et al., 2015.

claim: Ebony (e) is only expressed in neuropil glia.
source: Since we found another cluster of cells expressing Eaat1 and Gs2 in addition to ebony (e), and knowing that the last one is only expressed in neuropil glia, we annotated this cluster as astrocytes/neuropil glia.
evidence: The claim is stated as established knowledge in the text.

claim: Cortex/chiasm glia was identified by the expression of wrapper (wrapper) and hoepel1 (hoe1).
source: Then, cortex/chiasm glia was identified by the expression of wrapper (wrapper) (Konstantinides et al., 2018; Noordermeer et al., 1998) and hoepel1 (hoe1).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations to Konstantinides et al., 2018 and Noordermeer et al., 1998.

claim: Surface glia was characterized by the marker genes I'm not dead yet (Indy) and CG6126.
source: Lastly, surface glia was characterized by the following marker genes: I'm not dead yet (Indy) and CG6126 (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 6B showing expression of these genes.

claim: After 4 hours of starvation, the initial larval population was reduced approximately two times.
source: We observed that at this time point the initial larval population was reduced approximately two times, indicating the strong effect that starvation has on the survival rate (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 7—figure supplement 1 showing survival data.

claim: Both normal and starvation datasets overlap for most clusters containing cells from each condition.
source: We found that both datasets overlap for most clusters containing cells from each condition, with two clusters being present in only one condition.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text based on comparison of the two datasets.

claim: Two clusters were present in only one condition after starvation.
source: We found that both datasets overlap for most clusters containing cells from each condition, with two clusters being present in only one condition.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text based on comparison of the two datasets.

claim: After starvation, some cell-types were more strongly affected than others and changes in their transcriptional programs made them cluster separately.
source: This suggests that after starvation, some cell-types were more strongly affected than others and that the changes in their transcriptional programs made them cluster separately (Figure 7A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text as an inference from the clustering analysis and supported by Figure 7A.

claim: Two clusters missing after starvation were UNs 2 and Neurons X.
source: Among all the clusters, only two were missing after starvation: UNs 2 and Neurons X.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text based on comparison of normal and starved conditions.

claim: UNs 1 and UNs 2 both express genes involved in TORC1 signaling pathway: Repressed by TOR (REPTOR), REPTOR-binding partner (REPTOR-BP) and Thor.
source: The second cluster missing upon starvation was UNs 2, which showed an overall similarity with the non-altered UNs 1 cluster. Both expressed genes involved in TORC1 signaling pathway: Repressed by TOR (REPTOR), REPTOR-binding partner (REPTOR-BP) and Thor (Figure 7D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by Figure 7D showing expression of these genes.

claim: Hdc and unk form a complex and regulate cell cycle progression through binding TORC1 components, in response to nutrient intake.
source: In addition to these genes, we observed expression of hdc and unk, whose products form a complex and regulate cell cycle progression trough binding TORC1 components, in response to nutrient intake (Li et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Li et al., 2019.

claim: UNs 2 appear to be more sensitive to starvation conditions than the remaining cell types.
source: Therefore, UNs 2 appear to be more sensitive to starvation conditions than the remaining cell types, explaining their absence after starvation (Figure 7A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text as an inference from the absence of UNs 2 after starvation.

claim: A decreased number of hdc positive UNs was observed upon starvation.
source: We observed a decreased number of hdc positive UNs upon starvation, as suggested in silico.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text based on quantification of hdc expression.

claim: UNs display lower levels of the pan-neuronal marker elav compared to surrounding mature neurons.
source: In addition, these cells displayed lower levels of the pan-neuronal marker elav, in comparison to the surrounding mature neurons.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text based on analysis of elav expression levels.

claim: UNs can be characterized by a combination of high levels of hdc expression and low levels of elav expression.
source: These results suggest that UNs can be characterized by a combination of high levels of hdc expression an low levels of elav expression; and that in fact these group of cells were severely affected by the lack of nutrients (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text as an inference from expression analysis and supported by Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Neuroblasts are arrested in G0 or G2 phases of the cell-cycle in early larval stages.
source: In early larval stages neuroblasts are arrested in G0 or G2 phases of the cell-cycle (Otsuki and Brand, 2018) and a complex signaling mechanism between fat-body, glial cells and neuroblasts triggers their reactivation upon nutrient-sensing (Chell and Brand, 2010; Sousa-Nunes et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Otsuki and Brand, 2018, Chell and Brand, 2010, and Sousa-Nunes et al., 2011.

claim: A complex signaling mechanism between fat-body, glial cells and neuroblasts triggers neuroblast reactivation upon nutrient-sensing.
source: In early larval stages neuroblasts are arrested in G0 or G2 phases of the cell-cycle (Otsuki and Brand, 2018) and a complex signaling mechanism between fat-body, glial cells and neuroblasts triggers their reactivation upon nutrient-sensing (Chell and Brand, 2010; Sousa-Nunes et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Chell and Brand, 2010 and Sousa-Nunes et al., 2011.

claim: The cell-cycle heterogeneity in NPCs was maintained upon starvation, but the proportion among cell cycle phases was altered.
source: We observed that the above described cell-cycle heterogeneity was maintained upon starvation, but the proportion among cell cycle phases was altered.
